name: Scope
text: Assign the Content Strategy Lead to own a single, shared Decision Ledger with vetoes tied to clear, measurable project risks, such as legal or reputational concerns. This approach forces teams to commit to decisions upfront while providing a targeted escape hatch for high-stakes issues, making it the best option for cross-department alignment. The trade-off is that this approach requires upfront investment in defining and measuring project risks, which can be time-consuming. By accepting this trade-off, we can prevent the Decision Ledger from being exploited for minor gripes or last-minute renegotiations.

name: Scriv
text: The one-time veto credit still lets teams weaponize it—hoarding for "truly irreversible" risks that never come, then wasting it on minor squabbles when a real deadline looms. Instead, tie vetoes to *specific, time-bound project gates* (e.g., "veto only blocks the final 10% of a deliverable"). The Content Strategy Lead enforces this; if a team misuses it, the veto resets to a shared pool for the next quarter. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with one high-stakes project—if vetoes are misused, scrap the credit system entirely.

name: Reel
text: Assign the Content Strategy Lead to own a single, shared Decision Ledger with a *one-time, non-renewable veto credit per department per quarter*—no extensions, no renegotiations. This forces teams to commit to decisions upfront while giving them a last-resort escape hatch for truly irreversible conflicts. The trade-off is accepting that a department might burn its veto on a minor issue early, but that risk is outweighed by preventing endless mid-sprint renegotiations.

name: Scriv
text: Tying vetoes to measurable risks just shifts the problem—teams will game the metrics to justify vetoes, turning the Ledger into a bureaucratic nightmare. Instead, give each department a *one-time, irreversible veto* per quarter with a mandatory 24-hour written justification published in the Ledger. This forces them to own their vetoes publicly, making hoarding costly. Settle it by running a pilot for one quarter and measuring how often vetoes are used versus how often projects stall without them.

name: Chisel
text: Assign the Content Strategy Lead to own a single, shared Decision Ledger with a *one-time, non-renewable veto credit per department per quarter*—but only if the veto is triggered by a documented, irreversible risk to brand alignment or legal exposure. This forces teams to commit to decisions while giving them a last-resort escape hatch for truly existential stakes. The trade-off is that departments may delay decisions to preserve their veto, but the upfront documentation requirement makes that delay costly and transparent.

name: Sift
text: The one-time veto credit still lets teams weaponize it—hoarding vetoes for "irreversible risks" that never materialize, then deploying them when a project’s success matters most. Instead, require vetoes to cite *specific, pre-agreed failure criteria* in the Ledger upfront; if the risk doesn’t hit those metrics, the veto dies. That settles it: no gimmicks, just enforceable thresholds.
